title: Forty-Three Points and a Ten at Monte Rei
title_candidates: Forty-Three Points and a Ten at Monte Rei
Monte Rei Hands Out Three Personal Bests
Jon Baker's Eighty-Seven and Gregg Williams's Wobble
theme: On the third-hardest course TEG has rated, Monday produced the week's best Stableford score, an equalled course record and three personal bests.
opening_hook: Alex Baker signed for 43 points at Monte Rei on Monday, which is a fine afternoon's work anywhere and a remarkable one on a course that hands a TEG golfer 5.3 extra strokes before he has hit a ball — and he did it with a ten on his card at the 2nd.

round_story.subject: Alex Baker's 43 points, the best score of the day, assembled either side of a ten at the 2nd and a nine at the 12th
round_story.why_it_matters: It is the best round of the week so far on the hardest course of the four, it is Alex Baker's best gross score at Monte Rei by sixteen shots, and it lifts him to 110 and third place in the TEG 19 Trophy with one round left.
round_story.shape: Alex Baker came to Monte Rei off a 29-point Sunday that contained a ten, a nine, an eight and a seven, and on Monday he opened with a ten at the par-5 2nd. From the 6th he took 13 points in four holes, and a nine at the horseshoe 12th did not stop him; he came in with 43 points, fourteen better than the day before. The 98 gross is his best at Monte Rei, sixteen shots better than his previous visit this week.
headline_candidates: Alex Baker Takes Forty-Three From Monte Rei
Forty-Three Points With a Ten Aboard
Alex Baker Answers His Sunday Twenty-Nine
round_story.chosen_headline: Alex Baker Takes Forty-Three From Monte Rei
round_story.standfirst: Fourteen points better than Sunday and a sixteen-shot course best, achieved with a ten at the 2nd and a nine at the 12th still on the card.

race_story.subject: Jon Baker's record-equalling 87 stretches the Trophy lead to ten while Gregg Williams loses nine shots in four holes and keeps the Jacket by two
race_story.why_it_matters: Gregg Williams began the day five behind in the TEG 19 Trophy and four clear in the TEG 19 Green Jacket; he ended it ten behind and two clear, with one round to play.
race_story.shape: Jon Baker made a triple at the 2nd and doubles at the 3rd and 4th, then played the 11th to the 15th in level par for 16 points, the 13th and its promontory green included, before a seven at the 16th ended the run. His 87 equals the Monte Rei course record and takes the Trophy margin from five to ten. Gregg Williams dropped nine shots between the 9th and the 12th, saw Jon Baker draw level for the Jacket at the 15th, and needed a birdie at the last to finish the day two in front.
headline_candidates: Jon Baker Equals the Monte Rei Record
Gregg Williams Birdies the Last, Leads by Two
race_story.chosen_headline: Jon Baker Equals the Monte Rei Record
race_story.standfirst: Gregg Williams dropped nine shots in four holes around the turn and needed a birdie at the 18th to hold the Green Jacket lead at two.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson's 36 points and 97 gross, a fourteen-shot course best that cuts the Wooden Spoon gap from nine to three
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: John Patterson has been last in the TEG 19 Wooden Spoon since the 9th hole on Sunday, and he is now only three points behind David Mullin with eighteen holes left.
discovered_storylines.shape: John Patterson went double, double, double from the 2nd to the 4th and followed it with a triple at the 6th, which is the traditional opening to one of his less happy afternoons. He bogeyed the long 7th, the 8th and the 9th, then birdied the 5th-stroke-index 10th. The 36 points are eleven better than Sunday and the 97 gross beats his previous Monte Rei best by fourteen.
headline_candidates: John Patterson Closes the Spoon Gap
A Birdie at the Tenth Changes Monday
John Patterson Beats His Monte Rei Best
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: John Patterson Closes the Spoon Gap
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Eleven points better than Sunday and a 97 that improves his previous best here by fourteen, leaving David Mullin just three points above him.

race_state_note: The Trophy lead has not left Jon Baker since the 16th hole on Sunday, though Gregg Williams drew level with him at the 4th and again at the 6th on Monday without ever getting in front.
